abstract: Maintains precipitable water vapor monitoring and clear-sky integration records
system_message:
You are the Atmospheric physics lead (ATM). Your role is to maintain precipitable water vapor monitoring, clear-sky science integration records, and wind shear profiling across candidate high-altitude observatory sites.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Wind shear profiling（WIND）
information_points.content:
ATM-WIND-SI4：Anemometer network summary records across 12 consecutive months show that Cerro Toco Saddle reached a peak surface gust velocity of 35 m/s based on the maximum recorded 3-second gust speed.
ATM-WIND-F9F：Anemometer network summary records for candidate plateau ridgeline stations across 12 consecutive months show that Chajnantor North Terrace registered a peak surface gust velocity of 45 m/s based on the maximum recorded 3-second gust speed.
ATM-WIND-NK5：Anemometer network summary records across 12 consecutive months indicate that Pampa la Bola Plateau experienced a peak surface gust velocity of 25 m/s based on the maximum recorded 3-second gust speed.

information_points.title: Maintains precipitable water vapor monitoring and clear-sky integration records（CLIM）
information_points.content:
ATM-CLIM-V1R：For Pampa la Bola Plateau, radiometer atmospheric sounding records document a precipitable water vapor level of 2.0 mm (median zenith precipitable water vapor column thickness in the submillimeter observing band during winter observation months), and meteorological climatology models project 2,800 h of annual clear-sky science integration hours over one full calendar year of continuous atmospheric measurements.
ATM-CLIM-MCS：For Chajnantor North Terrace, radiometer atmospheric sounding records indicate a precipitable water vapor level of 1.1 mm (median zenith precipitable water vapor column thickness in the submillimeter observing band during winter observation months), while meteorological climatology models project 3,100 h of annual clear-sky science integration hours over one full calendar year of continuous atmospheric measurements.
ATM-CLIM-BLG：For Cerro Toco Saddle, radiometer atmospheric sounding records show a precipitable water vapor level of 1.1 mm (median zenith precipitable water vapor column thickness in the submillimeter observing band during winter observation months), alongside 3,400 h of annual clear-sky science integration hours projected over one full calendar year of continuous atmospheric measurements.
